en.intro: Duryodhana finishes naming the enemy and now turns to his own side. Listen to how he presents his commanders to Drona.
en.body: O best of the twice-born, note also our own chief warriors. I name them to remind you of our army. He calls Drona dvijottama, best of the twice-born, and then says he names these chiefs just to remind him of them. The word reminds him of the army he leads. Duryodhana lists Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa as the pillars of his army.

issues: borrowed: "He calls Drona dvijottama, twice-born, and then says he names these chiefs just to remind him. The teacher already knows them, yet Duryodhana must count and claim them aloud to feel the weight of his own army." (The notice presents the content of the NEXT verse (Bhishma, Karna, Kripa) as if it were in this verse. The Hindi notice (Hindi context/sandarbh) also incorrectly states that Drona already knows them and that Duryodhana lists them 'to remind him', which is an unsupported interpretation/detail.)

unsupported: "जिसमें उसकी घबराहट और अपने पक्ष को बड़ा दिखाने की इच्छा दोनों झलकती हैं।" (The source text provides no support for the claim that Duryodhana is feeling panic or has a desire to make his side look big. This is an unsupported psychological interpretation.)

wrong_fact: "next: Duryodhana lists Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa as the pillars of his army." (Verse 7 does not mention Bhishma, Karna, or Kripa. Verse 8 is the one that names them. The script attributes the content of the NEXT verse to the current verse.)

unsupported: "notice: The word reminds him of the army he leads." (The word 'संज्ञार्थं' means 'for the sake of recognition' or 'to remind', but the script invents the specific detail that it reminds Drona of 'the army he leads'. This specific interpretation is not found in the source text or the known Mahabharata story.)
